summary: The note argues that winter soups and stews made with seasonal produce are comforting, flavorful and nutritionally dense, citing dietitians and chefs who spoke at events between November 2023 and February 2024. It covers the science of seasonal eating, building a good soup base, root vegetables, legumes and leafy greens, and offers sample recipes and global variations.
one_line: A guide to hearty winter soups and stews built on seasonal produce, with expert tips on nutrition, stock, legumes, greens and recipes.
key_facts: Dr. Emily Ford, a dietician based in Chicago, said in a talk on November 12, 2023 that seasonal produce is related to higher nutrient density because it is harvested at peak ripeness.
The body's need for vitamin C, vitamin D and zinc rises in colder months because of their role in supporting the immune system.
Kale, Brussels sprouts, turnips and sweet potatoes are winter vegetables filled with immune-supporting nutrients.
Chef Robert Greene of the Winter Harvest Kitchen in Boston recommends a flavorful stock base (chicken, beef, vegetable or bone broth) and showed his technique in a workshop on December 15, 2023.
Bone broth adds depth and benefits like collagen to soup, according to Chef Robert Greene.
Ginger, garlic and bay leaves add flavor plus anti-inflammatory and antiviral properties to winter soups.
Carrots, parsnips and potatoes are stew staples that provide carbohydrates for energy and fiber for digestive health.

Dietician Annabelle Rodriguez, in her 'Winter Nutrition' seminar on January 20, 2024, said lentils, chickpeas and beans provide plant-based protein, fiber and complex carbohydrates and keep you full longer.
Swiss chard, collard greens and spinach thrive in cool weather and are low in calories but high in vitamins A, C and K, iron and antioxidants.
Linda Clarkson, a cookbook author, advised at her February 5, 2024 book release to add greens near the end of cooking to retain color, texture and nutrients.
Roasted butternut squash soup is a classic winter warmer rich in vitamins A and E, which support skin health.
Other suggested recipes are white bean and kale stew and beef and barley stew, the latter providing protein, iron and heart-healthy fiber.
Global examples include Moroccan tagine with cinnamon, cumin and coriander, and Japanese miso soup with winter greens and tofu.
